key_insight: Contextual tokens in multimodal diffusion transformers become readable internal representations of the emerging image, exposing scene semantics and details that grow over denoising.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical way to inspect, evaluate, and improve diffusion models by probing and aligning their hidden multimodal state rather than only the final output.
method: Train a lightweight bottleneck that maps intermediate contextual tokens into the input space of a frozen LLM.
Ask the LLM natural-language questions about the hidden state to decode what the model knows at each denoising step.
Use the readability signal to define Contextual Alignment, reinforcing visual-semantic information during training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that contextual information is decodable even with empty prompts, becomes more detailed over time, and correlates with higher human-preference scores.
watch_item: The approach depends on a learned probe and LLM-based interpretation, so decoded semantics may reflect the reader’s capacity and prompt design as much as the model’s true internal state.
paper_title: Learning to Read the Contextual Tokens in Diffusion Transformers
